items: Fix incorrect deletion of new endpoint during GC iteration when reusing ID from a previously GC'd endpoint (Backport PR cilium/cilium 49121, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 48905, @fristonio)
Fix ip6tables chain rename errors being silently ignored during iptables rule reconciliation. (Backport PR cilium/cilium 49333, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 49024, @maxskokov)

Fix restoration of terminating backends. If a terminating backend become active again during restart the backend was incorrectly kept as quarantined. (Backport PR cilium/cilium 48795, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 48763, @joamaki)
[ci] fix escaping in conformance ginkgo (Backport PR cilium/cilium 49121, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 48991, @nebril)

ci: cleanup disk space in documentation workflow (Backport PR cilium/cilium 48909, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 48427, @tklauser)
ci: Drop the empty floating tag line from CI image digests (Backport PR cilium/cilium 49121, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 49070, @aanm)
ci: fix CNI setup and readiness checks in the kubespray job (Backport PR cilium/cilium 49333, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 48927, @aanm)
ci: Give Envoy Embedded conformance a bigger runner (Backport PR cilium/cilium 49121, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 49018, @aanm)
ci: login to docker registry for downgrade image wait (Backport PR cilium/cilium 49121, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 48983, @nebril)
ci: Name runner variables after their Ubuntu release and let Renovate bump them (Backport PR cilium/cilium 49315, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 49065, @aanm)
ci: Skip redundant setup when base images already exist (Backport PR cilium/cilium 49315, Upstream PR cilium/cilium 47209, @HadrienPatte)

## Release Candidate 0 for v1.21.0

This is a **release candidate** and should be used for testing purposes only.

**⚠️ This is a pre-release. Do not use in production.**

### Changes

See the [release PR #7234](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/pull/7234) for the full changelog.

## [1.21.0](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/compare/v1.20.0...v1.21.0) (2026-10-14)


#### ⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

* **otelcol.receiver.kafka:** `otelcol.receiver.kafka` and `otelcol.exporter.kafka` `metadata > retry > max_retries` now defaults to `20` (was `3`) and is now actually applied. Upstream's Kafka client silently ignored it since the franz-go migration. `otelcol.exporter.kafka` now also applies `backoff`. ([#7366](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/issues/7366))
* **otelcol.connector.signaltometrics:** `otelcol.connector.signaltometrics` `error_mode` now defaults to `ignore` (was `propagate`). A failing OTTL expression now skips the record and logs the error instead of dropping the whole payload. Set `error_mode = "propagate"` to restore the previous behavior. ([#7366](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/issues/7366))
* **loki.write:** `loki.write` configurations that set `wal { enabled = true }` now fail to load unless Alloy runs with `--stability.level=experimental`. To keep using the WAL, add `--stability.level=experimental` to the `alloy run` command. To keep the default stability level, remove the `wal` block or set `enabled = false`. ([#7257](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/issues/7257))
* **loki.write:** Remove tenant label from metrics ([#7232](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/issues/7232))

#### Features 🌟

items.title: OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib v0.163.0
items.summary: The OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib contains everything in the opentelemetry-collector release, be sure to check the release notes there as well.
items.release_notes:
The OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib contains everything in the [opentelemetry-collector release](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/releases/tag/v0.163.0), be sure to check the release notes there as well.

## End User Changelog

### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `cmd/opampsupervisor`: The supervisor now fails to start when the deprecated `reports_remote_config` capability option is set to `true`. (#49763)
  Remove `reports_remote_config` from the supervisor config; `accepts_remote_config` enables both the AcceptsRemoteConfig and ReportsRemoteConfig OpAMP capabilities. The option will be removed in v0.165.0.
  
- `connector/failover`: Reject empty `condition.error.contains` values and fail over only for matching downstream errors (#44518)
  `condition.error.contains` now requires a list of non-empty strings.
- `exporter/signalfx`: Exclude generated `container_cpu_utilization` metric by default (#51906)
  This metric has been deprecated in favor of `container.cpu.usage`. If `container_cpu_utilization`
  is still required, please add it to the exporter's `include_metrics` configuration option as shown below.
  ```
  signalfx:
    include_metrics:
      - metric_name: container_cpu_utilization
  ```
  
- `extension/google_cloud_logentry_encoding`: Fix Cloud DNS query logs failing to decode when `vmInstanceId` is in exponent notation. `host.id` is now a string taken from `vmInstanceIdString` instead of an int taken from `vmInstanceId`. (#51552)
- `processor/redaction`: Keep every redaction summary attribute intact when data re-enters the processor (#50770)
  Only five of the fourteen summary attributes the processor writes survived a second redaction processor. When data
  passed through one, `redaction.allowed.keys`, `redaction.allowed.count` and the seven `redaction.body.*` attributes
  were treated as unknown keys, deleted, and reported in `redaction.redacted.keys`.
  
  The processor now treats all fourteen as its own bookkeeping rather than as user data, so they are no longer deleted,
  masked, obfuscated or counted as redacted, and the summary accumulates across chained processors as intended.
  Previously a `blocked_key_patterns` or `blocked_values` rule matching one of these attributes replaced the summary
  with a masked value, and with `redact_all_types` enabled it rewrote the `*.count` integers as strings, which made the
  running totals read back as zero at the next hop.
  
  Chaining two processors also reported the same attribute more than once: the allowed and ignored summaries
  describe the record as it currently stands, which every processor re-derives in full, so merging them with an
  upstream value counted one attribute twice. `redaction.allowed.keys` read `email,email` with
  `redaction.allowed.count` of 2 for a single allowed attribute. Those two outcomes now replace the upstream
  value, while the redacted and masked outcomes keep accumulating, because a removed key and an already masked
  value cannot be detected again.
  
  Two behaviour changes come with this, both of which can affect an existing chained configuration.
  
  A processor whose `summary` is not `debug` or `info` now claims no ownership of a summary it finds, so the ordinary
  allow list decides whether it survives. This lets a strict egress processor strip an upstream audit trail, which it
  could not do before. It also means a downstream processor with `allow_all_keys: false` now removes the five summary
  attributes it previously kept unconditionally, unless they are named in `allowed_keys` or `allow_all_keys` is set.
  `summary` is unset by default, which counts as silent, so a chained configuration that never sets it is affected.
  
  A key inside a log body named after a summary attribute is now redacted like any other unknown key. The processor
  only ever writes its summary to the record attributes, so such a key in a body carries user data.
  
- `receiver/postgresql`: Set the default scrape timeout to 60s to cancel blocked PostgreSQL queries. (#50757)
  Increase `timeout` for longer scrapes, or set `timeout: 0` to restore the unbounded behavior.
- `receiver/prometheus_simple`: Remove the long-deprecated `tls_enabled` and `tls_config` settings; use `tls` instead (#51895)
  `tls_enabled`/`tls_config` were deprecated in v0.55.0 in favor of the standard
  `tls` block (confighttp's TLS settings). Besides being long overdue, keeping both
  was a footgun: setting `tls_enabled: true` silently overrode any `tls` block.
  Migrate `tls_config` (`ca_file`/`cert_file`/`key_file`/`insecure_skip_verify`) to
  the equivalent fields under `tls`.
  
- `receiver/sql_server`: Performance counters read from the SQL Server `Databases` object on a direct database connection now carry the `sqlserver.database.name` resource attribute and no longer emit an unlabeled `_Total` aggregate, which changes the series identity of `sqlserver.database.backup_or_restore.rate`. (#51384)
  `sqlserver.database.backup_or_restore.rate` splits from one series into one per database, and the
  unlabeled series it previously reported is gone. Aggregate across `sqlserver.database.name` instead.
  This brings the direct database connection in line with the Windows performance counter path, which
  already discards the aggregate instance before recording.
  

### 🚩 Deprecations 🚩

- `receiver/sql_server`: Rename the `sqlserver` receiver to `sql_server`. The old `sqlserver` type remains available as a deprecated alias. (#45339)

### 🚀 New components 🚀

- `processor/adaptive_tail_sampling`: Promote the adaptive_tail_sampling processor to alpha stability and include it in the contrib distribution. (#49311)
- `processor/partitioning`: Add the initial skeleton for the partitioning processor. (#39199)
- `processor/rolling_span_latency`: Promote the rolling_span_latency processor to alpha stability and include it in the contrib distribution. (#50260)

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `connector/routing`: Validate OTTL conditions and statements during configuration. (#51748)
- `connector/service_graph`: Recognize current semantic-convention attributes (`peer.service.name`, `db.namespace`, `db.system.name`) alongside legacy keys when deriving peer and database-name dimensions. (#22095)
- `exporter/cassandra`: Add configuration validation and error case tests. (#51730)
- `exporter/clickhouse`: Add `database_engine` config to set the `ENGINE` used when creating the database, such as `Replicated`. (#51513)
  When `database_engine.name` is `Replicated`, `ON CLUSTER` is only applied to the `CREATE DATABASE` statement.
- `exporter/datadog`: Mark exporter/datadogexporter as unsupported on freebsd/amd64. (#15781)
- `exporter/datadog`: Move the `exporter.datadogexporter.AddUnits` feature gate to beta. Metric units are now sent to Datadog by default. (#15280)
- `exporter/elasticsearch`: Store OTLP exponential histograms in Elasticsearch's native exponential_histogram field (#51429)
  Enabled automatically in OTel mapping mode when connected to Elasticsearch 9.3.0 or later; disable via `version_detection.enabled: false`.
- `exporter/elasticsearch`: Log the connected Elasticsearch version and build flavor at startup (#51541)
  Adds `version_detection` (enabled by default); set `version_detection.enabled: false` to opt out.
- `exporter/kafka`: Add the trace context to Kafka record headers using the propagators configured in `service::telemetry::traces::propagators`. (#51078)
- `exporter/nats`: Implement core NATS publishing, so traces, metrics, and logs are published to per-signal subjects derived from OTTL value expressions. (#50735)
  JetStream durable publishing is not yet implemented; a configured `jetstream` block is rejected at startup until it lands.
  
- `exporter/splunk_hec`: Define the exporter's heartbeat metrics in metadata.yaml and generate them via mdatagen. (#49009)
- `extension/basicauth`: Support sourcing credentials from secret provider extensions, with rotation that does not restart the collector. (#48277)
  Configure with `htpasswd.secret_provider` (server) or `client_auth.secret_provider` (client).
  The referenced extension must implement the `SecretProvider` interface (`GetSecret` and `OnChange`).
  
- `extension/datadog`: Mark extension/datadogextension as unsupported on freebsd/amd64. (#15781)
- `extension/opamp`: Add a `socket` option under `server.ws` and `server.http` to dial the OpAMP server over a Unix domain socket (`transport: unix`) or Windows named pipe (`transport: npipe`). (#50603)
  When `socket` is set, the `endpoint` only supplies the URL scheme, request path, and Host
  header; its host and port are ignored.
  
- `extension/pebble_tail_storage`: Add `on_read_error` to choose between dropping a trace or returning the readable part when stored batches cannot be read or decoded. (#49906)
  The default is `drop_trace`. Take deletes the stored trace and returns an error, and the tail sampling processor drops the trace without a sampling decision.
  Set `on_read_error: return_partial` to keep the previous best-effort behavior, where Take returns the batches that could still be read.
  Two new metrics, `otelcol_extension_pebble_tail_storage_read_error_trace_drops` and `otelcol_extension_pebble_tail_storage_read_error_partial_returns`, count which policy ran.
  
- `internal/kafka`: Reuse cached AWS credentials across `AWS_MSK_IAM_OAUTHBEARER` token generations instead of resolving them on every SASL authentication. (#50038)
- `pkg/ottl`: Add the `pkg.ottl.functions.enableExperimental` feature gate, which must be enabled to use experimental OTTL functions. (#51564)
- `pkg/ottl`: Allow `keep_keys` to accept slice values from paths and converter expressions when the `pkg.ottl.functions.enableDynamicSliceArguments` feature gate is enabled. (#45980)
- `pkg/ottl`: Improve OTTL parse error diagnostics by reporting the line and column of the input where available. (#51680)
  Not all parse errors carry a position: errors that aggregate multiple statements, and some
  inner errors that didn't already carry one, are still returned without one. The exact
  wording and position of statement, condition, and value expression parse error messages
  has changed as a result. The position is exposed programmatically via the new experimental
  `xottl.Error` type.
  
- `pkg/ottl`: Add the beta `pkg.ottl.functions.enableDynamicSliceArguments` feature gate, which controls whether slice arguments of stable functions such as `Concat` accept paths and converters. (#51565)
- `pkg/stanza`: Optimize container parser operator by replacing CRI line and File path regexes with a hand-written parsers and caching log filepath metadata extraction, reducing CPU usage by ~70% on the container parser hot path (#41672)
- `pkg/stanza`: Add default scope name and version for stanza log entries without scope name (#51084)
  This introduces the `pkg.stanza.addDefaultScopeName` feature gate (currently in beta) to ensure Stanza log entries are assigned a default scope name and version when not explicitly provided.
  
- `processor/adaptive_tail_sampling`: Add `fleet_tracker` to divide each `adaptive_throughput` rule's `goal_throughput` by the live fleet member count reported by a `fleet_tracker` extension, making the goal a fleet-wide budget instead of a per-instance one. (#50577)
- `processor/akamaidetector`: Add `omit_detector_akamai` go build tag to omit detector at build time. (#47218)
- `processor/alibabaecsdetector`: Add `omit_detector_alibaba_ecs` go build tag to omit detector at build time. (#47218)
- `processor/azuredetector`: Add `omit_detector_azure` go build tag to omit detector at build time. (#47218)
- `processor/digitaloceandetector`: Add `omit_detector_digitalocean` go build tag to omit detector at build time. (#47218)
- `processor/dynatracedetector`: Add `omit_detector_dynatrace` go build tag to omit detector at build time. (#47218)
- `processor/groupbytrace`: Allow grouping spans by the service that emitted them within a trace (#50553)
  Adds an `emit_strategy` option that can be set to `service` to allow
  emitting spans sourced from a single service within a trace. In some
  setups this may allow spans to move more quickly through the processor
  while still permitting operations such as  RED metric generation,
  service discovery, etc. that require spans to be grouped by trace.
  
- `processor/hetznerdetector`: Add `omit_detector_hetzner` go build tag to omit detector at build time. (#47218)

- `processor/partitioning`: Implement logs partitioning. (#39199)

- `processor/scalewaydetector`: Add `omit_detector_scaleway` go build tag to omit detector at build time. (#47218)
- `processor/tail_sampling`: Move spans out of incoming batches instead of copying them, and declare that the processor mutates data. (#51920)
- `processor/tencentcvmdetector`: Add `omit_detector_tencent_cvm` go build tag to omit detector at build time. (#47218)
- `processor/upclouddetector`: Add `omit_detector_upcloud` go build tag to omit detector at build time. (#47218)

- `receiver/aws_cloudwatch`: Add `scope.name` and `scope.version` to logs and metrics. (#51333)
- `receiver/azure_blob`: Add a `compression` option to read gzip compressed blobs (#51412)
- `receiver/azure_monitor`: Add per-metric time grain overrides for Azure Monitor metric queries. (#51295)
- `receiver/google_cloud_spanner`: Add missing metrics to top minute transaction stats in `googlecloudspannerreceiver`. (#51272)
- `receiver/google_cloud_spanner`: Add top minute split stats metrics and `hide_split_stats_keys` logic in `googlecloudspannerreceiver`. All `split_stats/top/*` metrics gain the `split_start` and `split_limit` attributes with PII hiding support. (#51026)
- `receiver/google_cloud_spanner`: Add query_optimizer_versions and its value_type `int_slice` logic in `googlecloudspannerreceiver`. All `query_stats/top/*` metrics gain this new attribute. (#51219)
- `receiver/google_cloud_spanner`: Add missing execution metrics to total query stats in `googlecloudspannerreceiver`. (#51228)
- `receiver/google_cloud_spanner`: Add total minute transaction stats metrics to googlecloudspannerreceiver. (#51296)
- `receiver/kafka`: Add `partition_processing.max_in_flight.records` to run concurrent unmarshal-plus-Consume calls on one independent partition worker. (#51080)
  When `max_in_flight.records` is above 1, the worker always marks after processing. `message_marking.after: false` does not mark before Consume.
  
- `receiver/kubelet_stats`: Add optional k8s node pid limit and usage metrics. (#48926)
  Adds the following optional metrics to kubeletstatsreceiver:
  - k8s.node.pid.limit
  - k8s.node.pid.usage
  
- `receiver/mongodb`: Add assert, global lock queue, and write concern metrics (#51418)
  Adds `mongodb.assert.count`, `mongodb.global_lock.queue.count` and
  `mongodb.write_concern.wait.time`, all disabled by default.
  
- `receiver/mongodb`: Add query executor scan and collection scan metrics (#51060)
  Adds `mongodb.query_executor.index_key.scanned.count`,
  `mongodb.query_executor.document.scanned.count` and
  `mongodb.query_executor.collection_scan.count`, all disabled by default.
  
- `receiver/mongodb`: Report a loopback `server.address` as the collector host name, and enable `server.port` by default (#51633)
  When a scraped node reports a loopback address (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1`), `server.address` now
  reports the host name of the machine running the collector. `service.instance.id` is seeded from the same
  value and changes for those deployments. `server.port` was previously disabled by default; disable it with
  `resource_attributes.server.port.enabled: false`.
  
- `receiver/mysql`: Add row-count and database namespace context to the top query event (#51312)
- `receiver/oracledb`: Add support for Kerberos authentication via a new `auth_type` option and `kerberos` configuration block. (#50401)
  Set `auth_type: kerberos` and configure the `kerberos` block to authenticate using a keytab,
  credential cache, or password. Kerberos support is implemented in pure Go and requires no external
  libraries.
  
- `receiver/postgresql`: Add `connect_database` to configure which database the receiver connects to for cluster-wide statistics collection. (#50920)
- `receiver/prometheus_simple`: Restore the stability of the receiver from `unmaintained` to `beta` (#11504)
- `receiver/prometheus_simple`: Validate that `endpoint` is set and `collection_interval` is positive, so an invalid configuration is rejected at startup instead of failing later (#11504)
- `receiver/pulsar`: Add freebsd/amd64 as a supported build platform. (#15781)
  Updated the github.com/AthenZ/athenz dependency to v1.12.27 to enable
  freebsd/amd64 builds.
  
- `receiver/sql_server`: Add `sqlserver.db.edition` resource attribute. (#51414)
  Disabled by default. Opt in by setting `resource_attributes.sqlserver.db.edition.enabled: true` in the receiver config.
- `receiver/windows_event_log`: Promote Windows Event Log receiver to beta stability (#42167)

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `exporter/awsemf`: Drop a metric declaration with an invalid `metric_name_selectors` regex instead of panicking (#51115)
  An invalid regular expression in `metric_name_selectors` was passed to `regexp.MustCompile`,
  panicking during config validation. It is now compiled with `regexp.Compile` and the error is
  returned, so the declaration is dropped with a warning like an invalid `label_matchers` regex.
  
- `exporter/datadog`: Drop `instance` from the Azure App Service and Azure Functions running metrics in preparation for more accurate instance descriptions. (#51919)
  `otel.datadog_exporter.metrics.running.azureappservices` and `otel.datadog_exporter.metrics.running.azurefunctions` are now tagged only with `name`, `subscription_id`, and `resource_group`, and App Service metrics no longer get an `instance` tag.
  
- `exporter/file`: Fix race condition where a writer could be closed while still in use, causing data to be silently lost. (#49228)
  This will happen in `group_by` mode when `rotation` is not set.
- `exporter/file`: Reject `group_by.max_open_files` <= 0 and negative `rotation` values during config validation. (#51515)
- `extension/azure_encoding`: Do not emit 0-valued timeseries for aggregates (total, count, minimum, maximum, average) that are missing from the source Azure record (#50485)
  Diagnostic settings only export the aggregates a resource supports. A configured
  aggregation whose aggregate is absent from the record is now skipped instead of
  being coerced to 0.
  
- `extension/docker_observer`: Discover IPv6-only Docker endpoints and format their port targets correctly. (#50972)
- `extension/google_cloud_logentry_encoding`: Do not drop log entries with an unparseable `trace` or `spanId`, and accept a bare trace ID without the `projects/<project>/traces/` prefix. (#51666)
  Unparseable values are kept as the `gcp.trace` and `gcp.span_id` log record attributes.
- `pkg/faro`: Return an error instead of panicking when a log record contains a malformed `browser_brand_<N>` key (#51759)
- `pkg/faro`: Skip malformed `sdk_integrations` entries instead of panicking when translating logs to Faro payloads (#51484)
  An integration entry without a `:` separator, or a trailing comma, caused the Faro exporter to
  crash the collector. Such entries are now skipped. Versions that contain `:` are also no longer
  truncated.
  
- `pkg/ottl`: `Time` no longer treats a trailing strptime `%Z` as Zulu (UTC) when no location is given (#51416)
- `pkg/ottl`: Reject literal values that are not lists for slice arguments, such as `keep_keys(attributes, "http.method")` or `Concat("a", "-")`, at parse time instead of failing on every execution (#51833)
- `pkg/stanza`: Fix the `container` parser rejecting containerd logs whose timestamps use a UTC offset instead of `Z` when `format: containerd` is set. (#51284)
- `processor/adaptive_tail_sampling`: Forward an evicted trace on a detached context rather than the context of whichever request triggered the eviction, so its spans are no longer attributed to an unrelated client. (#51691)
  Components reading client.Info downstream, such as headers_setter with from_context, now see no client metadata for an evicted trace instead of the wrong request's.
- `processor/adaptive_tail_sampling`: Preserve original scope groups, scope metadata, and schema URLs when splitting spans by trace ID, including late spans handled by the decision cache. (#51461)
- `processor/cumulative_to_delta`: Fix ExponentialBuckets.Diff missing reset when old buckets precede current histogram offset (#51303)
- `processor/remotetap`: Fix a panic on shutdown (`close of nil channel`) when a websocket client had already disconnected before the processor shut down. (#51342)
- `processor/resource_detection`: Honor `fail_on_missing_metadata` also for the instance identity document and hostname lookups of the `ec2` detector (#50826)
  The `ec2` detector guarded only its initial `instance-id` lookup with `fail_on_missing_metadata`. The
  subsequent instance identity document and hostname lookups always returned their respective errors,
  regardless of the fail_on_missing_metadata setting.
  
  On clusters where the metadata service implements the EC2-compatible `meta-data` tree, but not the AWS-specific
  `dynamic/instance-identity` endpoints, this would lead to a crash on startup even with
  `fail_on_missing_metadata: false`. The `instance-id` lookup would succeed and then the identity document lookup would
  fail with HTTP 404. OpenStack Nova based clusters behave this way, so a collector configured with the `ec2` detector and
  `fail_on_missing_metadata: false` failed to start on those hosts rather than skipping the detector.
  
  The identity document lookup now honors the flag: when `fail_on_missing_metadata` is `false` and the endpoint
  responds with HTTP 404, the detector logs at debug level and returns an empty resource. Any other error is still
  returned, since it might be transient. When the flag is `true` the error is returned as before.
  
  The hostname lookup honors the flag as well: when `fail_on_missing_metadata` is `false`, the detector logs at
  debug level and returns the resource without the `host.name` attribute, instead of failing the detection or skipping
  the instance tags. When it is `true`, the error is returned.
  
- `receiver/azure_blob`: Return an error instead of panicking when an Event Hub message has no events or an unexpected blob subject (#51474)
  A malformed or unexpected Event Hub message could crash the collector. Such messages are now
  logged as errors and skipped, and events other than blob creation are ignored without being parsed.
  
- `receiver/azure_event_hub`: Do not emit 0-valued timeseries for aggregates (total, count, minimum, maximum, average) that are missing from the source Azure record (#50485)
  Diagnostic settings only export the aggregates a resource supports, e.g. a Standard
  Load Balancer exports total and count but no minimum/maximum. Missing aggregates are
  now skipped instead of being coerced to 0.
  
- `receiver/azure_event_hub`: Recreate the partition client after an `ownershiplost` error instead of polling a permanently detached link. (#51463)
  When another receiver with a higher epoch attached to the same partition and consumer group, the
  receiver logged `error receiving events` on every poll forever and never received data again.
  The partition client is now closed and reopened from the last received sequence number with exponential backoff.
  
- `receiver/cloud_foundry`: Do not emit partially initialized log records for unsupported log types. (#51517)
- `receiver/googlecloudmonitoring`: Emit data points in chronological order to prevent data loss in downstream processors. (#51641)
- `receiver/host_metrics`: Reject negative `metadata_collection_interval` values during configuration validation. (#51640)
- `receiver/kafka`: Fix records from healthy partitions being dropped when a poll also contains a fetch error. (#51852)
- `receiver/mysql`: Report `mysql.index.io.wait.count` and `mysql.index.io.wait.time` under the correct `operation` attribute (#49597)
  The `mysql.index.io.wait.count` and `mysql.index.io.wait.time` metrics were reported under the
  wrong `operation` attribute (for example, delete counts appeared under `operation=update`). Each
  datapoint is now reported under its correct operation.
  
- `receiver/postgresql`: Add `postgresql.userid` to `db.server.top_query` and `db.server.query_plan`, and key the top-query counter cache and EXPLAIN plan cache on it instead of `postgresql.rolname`. Fixes a case where two dropped database roles could be reported under each other's counters or query plan, and keeps counter deltas continuous across a role rename. (#51319)
- `receiver/prometheus_remote_write`: Attach exemplars once, to the series that sent them, rather than to every metric built from the same labels. (#50334, #50546)
- `receiver/splunk_enterprise`: Fixes recorded value for RollingRestartStatus metric (#51866)
- `receiver/sql_server`: Fix missing metrics when using direct SQL Server connection - `sqlserver.lock.wait_time.avg`, `sqlserver.transaction.rate`, `sqlserver.page.operation.rate`, `sqlserver.page.lazy_write.rate`, and `sqlserver.transaction_log.growth.count` now emit values on non-Windows platforms and when the receiver is configured with a direct database connection. (#51384)
  All of these except `sqlserver.transaction_log.growth.count` report no
  data point on the first scrape, since they are calculated from the change in their counters between scrapes.
  
- `receiver/sql_server`: `sqlserver.session.duration` now reports whole seconds since login instead of milliseconds, fixing a 25-day overflow in `total_elapsed_time`. (#51419)
- `receiver/sql_server`: Fix direct connection queries returning no data when `instance_name` is set to a named instance (#50773)
  The direct connection queries filtered rows with `@@SERVERNAME = '<instance_name>'`. On a named
  instance `@@SERVERNAME` returns `<host>\<instance>`, which never matches the bare instance name,
  so every query returned zero rows and no metrics were emitted. The filter was also redundant:
  a connection is scoped to a single instance and its DMVs only expose that instance. It has been
  removed. `instance_name` remains in use for the Windows performance counter collection path.
  
- `receiver/sql_server`: Fix direct-connection performance counter rate metrics to emit per-second rates instead of cumulative counter values. (#50772)
  The `sqlserver.page.buffer_cache.free_list.stalls.rate` metric value type changes from int to double so fractional rates can be represented.
  
- `receiver/statsd`: Close the TCP connection when the client disconnects and bound the size of an unterminated line, fixing a per-connection file descriptor leak and an unbounded memory growth path in the TCP transport. (#50123)
- `receiver/webhook_event`: Validate that `path` and `health_path` begin with a leading `/` so the collector fails at config load instead of panicking at startup. (#50893)
  A `path` or `health_path` without a leading `/` caused `httprouter` to panic in `Start()`,
  after the collector had already bound its telemetry port. The panic left the port held, so every
  restart attempt failed with `bind: address already in use`.
  
- `receiver/yang_grpc`: Apply the configured `security.allowed_clients` and `security.rate_limiting` settings to the `MdtDialout` streaming RPC, which previously did not enforce either. (#0)
- `scraper/network`: Fix incorrect Linux TCP state names (`FIN_WAIT_1`/`FIN_WAIT_2`) used by the networkscraper, which never matched real connection states. (#51271)

<!-- previous-version -->

## API Changelog

### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `pkg/ottl`: `FunctionContext` and the `Standard*Getter` structs can no longer be initialized with unkeyed struct literals. (#47305)
- `pkg/ottl`: Move the experimental lambda expression Go API into the `pkg/ottl/xottl` module so it is excluded from OTTL's stability guarantees. (#51566)
  `LambdaExpression`, `LambdaActivation`, and `NewTestingLambdaExpression` moved to
  `github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pkg/ottl/xottl`. `LocalIdentifierDecl` and
  `LambdaExpression.Formals` were removed.
  
- `pkg/ottl`: Move the experimental `SliceGetter` API to the `xottl` module. (#51565)
  `ottl.SliceGetter`, `ottl.GetLiteralValues`, `ottl.GetScalarLiteralValues`, and `ottl.NewTestingSliceGetter` are now in `xottl`.

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `connector/routing`: Create `With*Functions` factory options to allow custom OTTL functions registration. (#51709)
- `pkg/ottl`: Improve OTTL parse error diagnostics by reporting the line and column of the input where available. (#51680)
  Not all parse errors carry a position: errors that aggregate multiple statements, and some
  inner errors that didn't already carry one, are still returned without one. The exact
  wording and position of statement, condition, and value expression parse error messages
  has changed as a result. The position is exposed programmatically via the new experimental
  `xottl.Error` type.
  
- `pkg/ottl`: Add `WithCache` option to the `ottlotelcol` `TransformContext`. (#51652)
- `pkg/pdatatest`: Add pmetricassert numeric comparison operators (#48470)

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `pkg/ottl`: Preserve the distinction between nil and empty slices in the `xottl` `GetScalarLiteralValues` and `GetLiteralValues` helpers. (#51814)

### Images and binaries here: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/tag/v0.163.0

## End User Changelog

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `cmd/builder`: Add `dist.resource.detection.detectors` to the builder config, letting distributions opt into a smaller set of resourcedetectionprocessor detectors via generated go build tags. (#16075)
- `cmd/mdatagen`: Generate exporter queue/batch sender defaults from an opt-in `sending_queue` field in metadata.yaml. See the [batching migration RFC](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/rfcs/batching-migration.md). (#15963)
  Declaring `sending_queue` is opt-in; an exporter that omits it is unaffected until it explicitly opts in one at a time during Phase 2 of the migration. Set MDATAGEN_SENDING_QUEUE_OPT_OUT=true to generate the standard default for every undeclared exporter while auditing a whole repository.
- `pkg/pprofile`: Implement Profiles development-version metadata in the OTLP receiver and exporters. (#16147, #16009)
  The receiver rejects malformed, repeated, or unsupported versions before decoding.
  OTLP exporters send the version associated with their compiled-in Profiles schema.
  The version is not configurable, and existing clients without metadata identify
  the initial development version.
  

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `cmd/mdatagen`: Replace the O(n) scan in generated `recordDataPoint` with an O(1) hash lookup, fixing an O(n²) cost per scrape when many data points land on one resource. (#15912)
- `cmd/mdatagen`: When both migration gates are enabled, only the latest metric with its v1 attributes is emitted (legacy attributes are no longer included). (#15979)
- `pkg/exporterhelper`: Fix sending queue deadlocks when blocked offers are cancelled with block_on_overflow enabled. (#15700)
- `pkg/exporterhelper`: Drop only the oversized profile when splitting a profiles batch, instead of discarding every profile queued behind it (#16087)
  Same fix as
- `pkg/exporterhelper`: Drop only the oversized span when splitting a traces batch, instead of discarding every span queued behind it (#16087)
  Same fix as
- `pkg/pprofile`: Use the profiles dictionary for resource and scope attribute strings sent over OTLP/gRPC. (#15861)

items.title: Versioned metrics: Shipping the first Release Candidate metrics in hostmetrics
items.summary: OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib v0.160.0 adds the ability to emit release candidate (RC) process semantic conventions metrics to the hostmetrics receiver’s process scraper, the last stage before a stable v1. The System SIG has worked on this for the better part of a year, and we think that the process metrics are in a good shape – but RC exists so the community can prove that. If you collect process metrics, we’d like you to try the new versioned output and tell us what breaks.

items.title: OpenTelemetry Operator v0.161.0
items.release_notes:
## 0.161.0

### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `opamp`: Use the Kubernetes cluster ID to compute standalone OpAMP Bridge agent instance IDs. (#5689)
  - Existing standalone agents will report new instance IDs after upgrade.
  - The bridge now requires the "get" permission on the "kube-system" namespace to read the cluster ID.
  
- `collector`: Remove the deprecated `--create-rbac-permissions` CLI flag. RBAC permission creation is now exclusively autodetected at startup. (#2588)
  The flag was deprecated in v0.88.0. The operator now always autodetects whether its service account can create ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings.

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `collector`: Add `revisionHistoryLimit` field to OpenTelemetryCommonFields to control the number of old ReplicaSets retained for Deployment and StatefulSet workloads, and for the TargetAllocator Deployment. (#0)
- `collector`: Skip the automatic `GOMEMLIMIT` and `GOMAXPROCS` environment variables when the collector config enables the `cgroup_runtime` extension. (#5651)
  The extension sets both variables from the cgroup limits and does nothing when they are already present.
  The deprecated `cgroupruntime` type name is recognized as well.
  Each variable is skipped only while its `gomemlimit.enabled` or `gomaxprocs.enabled` setting is true.
  
- `collector, target allocator`: Add `imagePullSecrets` to the OpenTelemetryCollector and TargetAllocator CRs, passed through to the pod spec of the generated workloads. A target allocator embedded in an OpenTelemetryCollector uses the collector's `imagePullSecrets`. (#4376)
- `collector`: Register the `webhook_event` receiver (alias `webhookevent`) so the operator derives its Service port from `endpoint`, which the receiver requires, and rejects a configuration that omits it. (#5631)

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `collector`: Fix the collector defaulting webhook panicking when `receivers` or `exporters` is missing. (#5735)
  The request is now rejected by CRD validation, as it already was when no component defaults apply.
- `target allocator`: Honor the cumulative temporality preference for counters bridged from the Prometheus registry in OTLP self-telemetry. (#5700)
  Bridged counters, such as the Prometheus service discovery metrics, were converted to delta regardless of
  `temporality_preference`. They are now converted only when the preference selects delta for counters
  (`delta` or `low_memory`), and are exported as cumulative otherwise.
  
- `target allocator`: Keep the Kubernetes API server addresses in the target allocator NetworkPolicy up to date. (#5551)
  The operator now watches the EndpointSlices of the `default/kubernetes` Service and updates the target allocator
  NetworkPolicy when they change, instead of using the addresses discovered once at operator startup.
  Addresses which disappear from the EndpointSlices remain allowed for 5 minutes, to tolerate transient changes.
  The NetworkPolicy also allows egress to the `kubernetes` Service ClusterIP, and uses correct CIDRs for IPv6 addresses.
  The operator now requires the `watch` permission on `endpointslices` in the `discovery.k8s.io` API group.
  
- `operator`: Fix the `--tls-min-version` CLI flag being ignored because it was matched against the wrong flag name. (#3565)
- `sidecar`: Prevent sidecar injection into invalid pods with zero regular containers (#5737)
  Pods without containers are invalid in Kubernetes. Skipping injection allows Kubernetes to reject the invalid Pod rather than mutating it into a valid one.

### Components

* [OpenTelemetry Collector - v0.161.0](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/releases/tag/v0.161.0)
* [OpenTelemetry Contrib - v0.161.0](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/releases/tag/v0.161.0)
* [Java auto-instrumentation - v2.32.0-1](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/releases/tag/v2.32.0)
* [.NET auto-instrumentation - v1.17.0-2](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet-instrumentation/releases/tag/v1.17.0)
* [Node.JS - v0.78.0-6](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/releases/tag/experimental%2Fv0.78.0)
* [Python - v0.66b1-2](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-contrib/releases/tag/v0.66b1)
* [Go - v0.24.0](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-instrumentation/releases/tag/v0.24.0)
* [ApacheHTTPD - 1.0.4-2](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-cpp-contrib/releases/tag/webserver%2Fv1.0.4)
* [Nginx - 1.0.4-2](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-cpp-contrib/releases/tag/webserver%2Fv1.0.4)

items.title: VictoriaMetrics v1.154.0
items.release_notes:
## [v1.154.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.154.0)

Released at 2026-10-12

**Update Note 1:** [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): setups with two chained `vmauth` instances, where the first one authenticates requests via `users` and the second one proxies them via `unauthorized_user` (for example, `VMDistributed` or `VMCluster` managed by [VictoriaMetrics operator](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/operator/)), get an extra 2-3 seconds delay for every request. This is because the second `vmauth` receives the `Authorization` header forwarded by the first one and treats it as an invalid auth token. Upgrade to the [v1.154.1](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/master/docs/victoriametrics/changelog/CHANGELOG.md#v11541) release, where requests aren't delayed if no `users` are configured, or remove the `Authorization` header at the first `vmauth` with `headers: ["Authorization:"]`. See [#11774](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11774).

**Update Note 2:** `vmstorage` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): `/admin/tenants` requests without `start` and `end` query args (or with zero values) can cause excessive memory usage and OOM crashes of `vmstorage`. Such requests are issued automatically by [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui) when it is opened via `vmselect`. This is because `vmstorage` [no longer switches to the global index](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/commit/742778ebf1) for queries with long time ranges, so it scans per-day indexes for every day in the whole retention concurrently. Upgrade to [v1.155.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.155.0), or roll back to [v1.153.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.153.0). See [#11791](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11791).

**Update Note 3:** [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and `vmstorage` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): queries and requests to `/api/v1/series`, `/api/v1/labels` and `/api/v1/label/.../values` with long time ranges can cause excessive memory usage and OOM crashes. This is because VictoriaMetrics [no longer switches to the global index](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/commit/742778ebf1) for searches with long time ranges, so it scans per-day indexes for every day in the requested time range concurrently. Upgrade to [v1.155.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.155.0), or roll back to [v1.153.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.153.0). See [#11791](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11791).

**Update Note 4:** `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): `-search.skipSlowReplicas` causes excessive connection churn between `vmselect` and `vmstorage`, increased `vmstorage` CPU usage and `cannot process vmselect conn ... write: broken pipe` errors in `vmstorage` logs. This is because `vmselect` now [cancels requests](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11355) to slow replicas by closing connections to `vmstorage` instead of reusing them. Disable `-search.skipSlowReplicas` or roll back to [v1.153.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.153.0) until the fix is available. See [#11771](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11771).

* SECURITY: upgrade Go builder from Go1.27.1 to Go1.27.2. See [the list of issues addressed in Go1.27.2](https://github.com/golang/go/issues?q=milestone%3AGo1.27.2%20label%3ACherryPickApproved).
* SECURITY: [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): slow down requests with invalid auth tokens even if `unauthorized_user` has URLs configured. Previously, such requests were proxied to `unauthorized_user` without delay, which allowed brute-forcing auth tokens. See [GHSA-rpfx-hrcp-f73x](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/security/advisories/GHSA-rpfx-hrcp-f73x).
* SECURITY: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): prevent [cross-site scripting (XSS)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-site_scripting) on Metric Relabling Debug, Query Analyzier, and Dashboards pages. See [GHSA-m2x2-9xpq-mmq5](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/security/advisories/GHSA-m2x2-9xpq-mmq5).

* FEATURE: [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/),`vminsert` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/) and [Single-node VictoriaMetrics](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/): add `/influx/ping` endpoint, which returns the `X-Influxdb-Version` HTTP header. Some [InfluxDB](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/integrations/influxdb/) clients, such as the Jenkins InfluxDB plugin, read the server version from this endpoint. See [#11663](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11663). Thanks to @Vandit1604 for contribution.
* FEATURE: [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): add `oidc.auth_params` option to [SSO](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/#single-sign-on-sso) config for passing additional query parameters to the IdP authentication request, e.g., `hd` for narrowing the Google account chooser to a single domain. Combine it with `match_claims` to enforce the domain restriction. See [these docs](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/#sso-authentication-request-parameters) for more examples of `oidc.auth_params` usage.
* FEATURE: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and `vmstorage` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): abort incoming requests when a client disconnects and during graceful shutdown. See [#11472](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11472).
* FEATURE: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): cancel query requests if client disconnects. See [#11355](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11355).

* BUGFIX: all VictoriaMetrics components: correctly configure TCP keep-alive active probes. See [#11695](github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11695).
* BUGFIX: all VictoriaMetrics components: properly match regexps that start with an alternation or a character class and continue with `.*foo.*` or `.+foo.+`, for example `(a|b).*foo.*`. Previously the leading part was ignored when matching [relabeling](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/relabeling/) `regex` and `if` filters and [stream aggregation](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/) `match` filters, so such rules matched more series than intended. See [#11712](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11712). Thanks to @dblackdblack for contribution.
* BUGFIX: [alerts](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/master/deployment/docker/rules): fix  incorrect results for `TooHighChurnRate` and `TooHighSlowInsertsRate` in [cluster alerting rules](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/master/deployment/docker/rules/alerts-cluster.yml). Previously due to incorrect expressions, these rules stayed inactive since [v1.108.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.108.0) and could produce false positives since [v1.153.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.153.0). See [#11670](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11670). Thanks to @transacid for contribution.
* BUGFIX: [stream aggregation](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/): properly add timeseries for [increase](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/configuration/#increase), [increase_prometheus](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/configuration/#increase_prometheus), [total](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/configuration/#total) and [total_prometheus](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/configuration/#total_prometheus) aggregation functions when `enable_windows: true` is set. See [#11707](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11707). Thanks to @Hoipang for contribution.
* BUGFIX: [vmalert](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmalert/): keep using notifiers from the previously applied [notifier configuration file](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmalert/#notifier-configuration-file) if the updated config fails to start, for example due to a temporary service discovery error, and retry applying it on the next reload. Previously, vmalert stopped the old notifiers before starting the new ones, so a failed reload left vmalert with no or only some notifiers, and alert notifications were silently not delivered until the file changed or vmalert restarted. See [#11645](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11645).
* BUGFIX: [vmalert](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmalert/): copy alert labels before applying `alert_relabel_configs` from the [notifier configuration file](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmalert/#notifier-configuration-file), preventing different alertmanagers from affecting each other's labels. See [#11676](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11676).
* BUGFIX: [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/) and [vmalert](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmalert/): set the `Host` HTTP request header to the resolved DNS SRV target instead of the SRV name when the url uses the `srv+` prefix. Previously requests could fail at reverse proxies and load balancers, which route by the `Host` header. See [#8965](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/8965).
* BUGFIX: [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): fixes rare data corruption on HTTP request retries. See [#11508](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11508).
* BUGFIX: [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): fix [SSO](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/#single-sign-on-sso) login failure `Invalid state parameter` caused by a race condition when multiple concurrent unauthenticated requests each set their own CSRF cookie. See [#10278-comment](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/10278#issuecomment-5862232663) and [#11656](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11656).
* BUGFIX: [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): fix misleading `missing 'Authorization' request header` response for [JWT-authenticated](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/#jwt-token-auth-proxy) users when the requested path does not match any `url_map`. Now it correctly returns `400 Bad Request` with `missing route` error, matching the behavior of [Basic Auth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/#basic-auth-proxy) and [Bearer-token](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/#bearer-token-auth-proxy) users. See [#11523](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11523).
* BUGFIX: [vmbackup](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmbackup/) and [vmbackupmanager](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmbackupmanager/): add `-s3SkipTaggingDirective` command-line flag for S3-compatible storage that rejects the `x-amz-tagging-directive` and `x-amz-tagging` headers. See [#11562](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11562).
* BUGFIX: `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): add missing `accountID`, `projectID` and `multiTenant` fields to `topByAvgMemoryUsage` results at `/api/v1/status/top_queries`. See [#11640](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11640).
* BUGFIX: `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): prevent rare resource leak if `-search.skipSlowReplicas` flag is set. See [#11551](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11551).
* BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): properly execute `group_left(...)` and `group_right(..)` queries when the join is then combined with another selector. See [#11490](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11490).
* BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and `vmstorage` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): prevent possible crash with `cannot decompress zstd data...` panic on `darwin`, `windows`, `freebsd`, `openbsd`, `linux/arm`, `linux/ppc64le`, `linux/386`, `linux/s390x`, and `-pure` builds. The `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` builds are not affected. See [#11683](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11683).
* BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/): properly apply `-streamAggr.enableWindows` command-line flag to [stream aggregation](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/) rules. Previously, the flag was ignored by aggregation rules defined in `-streamAggr.config` and was applied only during config validation with `-dryRun` and to the standalone deduplication configured via `-streamAggr.dedupInterval`. See [#11717](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11717).
* BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and `vmstorage` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): properly release memory after historical [data backfilling](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/#backfilling). Previously storage kept 8MiB*CPU memory for each month of ingested data until restart. See [#11672](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11672). Thanks to @mars71003219 for contribution.
* BUGFIX: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): prevent overriding the `serverUrl`, `tenantId`, `theme`, and `isDarkTheme` settings via query parameters. See [#11485](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11485#issuecomment-5779024739).

See 11645.

items.title: Prometheus and OpenTelemetry interoperability in 2026: Survey results
items.summary: We ran a survey asking users of OpenTelemetry and Prometheus how they collect, process, and store metrics. The goal was to understand, with real usage data rather than assumptions, how far the ecosystem has moved and whether the interoperability still causes friction. Key takeaways Interoperability has measurably improved since our 2024 survey : the average ease-of-use rating rose from 3.1 to 3.6, the equivalent of one in two respondents rating a whole category higher, and the share of respondents finding the two hard to use together fell from 29% to 10%. In infrastructure instrumentation, Prometheus exporters remain the most-used method (72%) with OTel receivers close behind (57%), and nearly half of respondents run both at once rather than migrating from one to the other. In application instrumentation, OTel SDKs are the most-used method at 65% with Prometheus SDKs at 52%, and 41% use only the OTel style of application instrumentation. items.title: OTel-Native by Design - Building Products That Export to Any Observability Stack
items.summary: With contributions from Dan Gomez Blanco (New Relic). If you’re building self-hosted software or a SaaS product, your users will eventually ask to send logs, traces, and metrics to their own observability stack, whether to satisfy compliance, manage costs, or centralize all their observability data in one place. Locking them into your built-in dashboards or limiting exports to certain vendors creates unnecessary friction. Instead, supporting export to any OpenTelemetry (OTel)-compatible backend is a vendor-neutral, future-proof practice that gives users the freedom to choose their observability stack.

items.title: Jaeger v2.22.0
items.summary: Backend Changes
items.release_notes:
### Backend Changes

#### ⛔ Breaking Changes

* Fix(es): configure numeric attribute indexing instead of gating it ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9694](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9694))
* Refactor(es): give the span index its own options type ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9693](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9693))
* Fix(remote-storage): configure the service from one confmap-decoded file ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9699](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9699))
* Fix(es): honor index-prefix in dependencies/sampling legacy templates ([@zarna1parekh](https://github.com/zarna1parekh) in [#9684](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9684))
* Feat(es): promote the native trace summaries gate to stable ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9609](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9609))
* Feat(query): promote the structured filters feature gate to beta ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9607](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9607))
* Feat(query): give span searches their own query interceptor hooks ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9597](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9597))
* Feat(es): promote the omitparentspanidreference gate to beta ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9586](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9586))

#### ✨ New Features

* Feat(es): declare span search and pagination ([@baroquebobcat](https://github.com/baroquebobcat) in [#9729](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9729))
* Feat(memory): execute caller-selected span ordering ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9672](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9672))
* Feat(query): expose span ordering in api v3 ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9671](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9671))
* Feat(storage): forward span ordering over grpc ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9670](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9670))
* Feat(query): validate and bind span ordering ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9669](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9669))

#### 🐞 Bug fixes, Minor Improvements

* Fix(memory): skip same-service parents when building dependency links ([@lopster568](https://github.com/lopster568) in [#9090](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9090))
* Fix(es-rollover): reject unknown --unit values in lookback (takeover #9442) ([@jkowall](https://github.com/jkowall) in [#9732](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9732))
* Fix(jaegerquery,remotestorage): remove nil error wrap in start() ([@g-k-s-03](https://github.com/g-k-s-03) in [#8882](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/8882))
* Fix(memory): use read locks for read-only samplingstore methods ([@shayannab](https://github.com/shayannab) in [#9005](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9005))
* Fix(es): return an error for a nil predicate instead of panicking ([@RudraDudhat2509](https://github.com/RudraDudhat2509) in [#9709](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9709))
* Feat(es): break span sort ties on the backing index and document id ([@baroquebobcat](https://github.com/baroquebobcat) in [#9720](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9720))
* Feat(es): search spans in the core reader ([@baroquebobcat](https://github.com/baroquebobcat) in [#9704](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9704))
* Fix(release): re-enable slsa provenance with valid tag reference (#9046) ([@Kartikupadhyay44](https://github.com/Kartikupadhyay44) in [#9702](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9702))
* Feat(es): wire span search through the elasticsearch reader ([@baroquebobcat](https://github.com/baroquebobcat) in [#9700](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9700))
* Feat(es): lower starttime comparisons into filter (rfc 0016 m4) ([@baroquebobcat](https://github.com/baroquebobcat) in [#9697](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9697))
* Fix(ai-sidecar): point default mcp url to query port 16686 ([@rautaditya2606](https://github.com/rautaditya2606) in [#9658](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9658))
* Fix(memory): validate positive maxtraces ([@DsThakurRawat](https://github.com/DsThakurRawat) in [#9634](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9634))
* Fix(es): gate attribute ordering separately from typed attribute indexing ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9690](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9690))
* Fix(query): answer capability refusals with unimplemented instead of invalidargument ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9685](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9685))
* Fix(storage): apply timeout to grpc storage calls ([@anishmehta24](https://github.com/anishmehta24) in [#9638](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9638))
* Fix(remotesampling): reject non-positive leader election lease refresh intervals ([@pujitha24](https://github.com/pujitha24) in [#9647](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9647))
* Fix(es): give the sync batch size half of the bulk cap as headroom ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9645](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9645))
* Fix(jptrace): tracesdata.marshaltosizedbuffer writes to buffer head instead of tail ([@om7057](https://github.com/om7057) in [#9629](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9629))
* Fix(config): batch and block on overflow in the kafka ingester configurations ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9624](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9624))
* Fix(query): copy the whole pagination struct before clamping ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9618](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9618))
* Fix(query): clamp the page size on a copy rather than through the caller pointer ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9617](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9617))
* Feat(query): admit rfc 0014 pagination into the query path ([@om7057](https://github.com/om7057) in [#9450](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9450))
* Feat(es): support span.traceid and span.spanid in structured filters ([@prajak002](https://github.com/prajak002) in [#9610](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9610))
* Fix(anonymizer): write ui trace file when max-spans-count is reached ([@DsThakurRawat](https://github.com/DsThakurRawat) in [#9567](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9567))
* Feat(query): add findspans to the query service ([@baroquebobcat](https://github.com/baroquebobcat) in [#9581](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9581))
* Fix(mcp): reject negative durations in search_traces before querying ([@pujitha24](https://github.com/pujitha24) in [#9575](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9575))
* Fix(mcp): back off to a rune boundary when truncating read_skill ([@om7057](https://github.com/om7057) in [#9589](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9589))
* Fix(query): refuse a trace filter that a later interceptor drops ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9606](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9606))
* Fix(es): prevent service-operation key collisions ([@SaadShakeel1](https://github.com/SaadShakeel1) in [#9440](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9440))
* Fix(elasticsearch): support ordered built-in text filters ([@alishair7071](https://github.com/alishair7071) in [#9477](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9477))
* Fix(samplingstore): propagate write errors in insertthroughput and insertprobabilitiesandqps ([@shashankvarma499](https://github.com/shashankvarma499) in [#9533](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9533))
* Fix(es): retry failed writes in the synchronous kafka ingester config ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9593](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9593))
* Feat(query): add the rfc 0014 pagination contract to tracestore ([@om7057](https://github.com/om7057) in [#9570](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9570))
* Fix(es-rollover): reject non-positive unit-count in lookback action ([@DsThakurRawat](https://github.com/DsThakurRawat) in [#9568](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9568))
* Test(jaegerquery): add labeled trace fixtures and e2e coverage for the built-in skills ([@SoumyaRaikwar](https://github.com/SoumyaRaikwar) in [#9263](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9263))
* Fix(query): prevent archiving archive-only traces ([@jkowall](https://github.com/jkowall) in [#9391](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9391))
* Fix(es): do not double the separator when index-prefix already ends in "-" ([@pujitha24](https://github.com/pujitha24) in [#9551](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9551))
* Fix(tracegen): validate attr-keys and attr-values to prevent divide-by-zero ([@shashankvarma499](https://github.com/shashankvarma499) in [#9545](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9545))

#### 🚧 Experimental Features

* Feat(storage): add findspans and search pagination to the memory backend ([@om7057](https://github.com/om7057) in [#9611](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9611))
* Feat(storage): add the rfc 0014 page token that paginating readers return ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9655](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9655))
* Feat(query): add the api_v3 findspans handler and http route ([@om7057](https://github.com/om7057) in [#9613](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9613))
* Feat(es): add the jaeger_storage_writer connector to dead-letter rejected spans ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9604](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9604))
* Feat(es): report terminally rejected bulk items in a typed error ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9598](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9598))
* Feat(query): rfc 0016 m2 - pt 1 - add searchspans to capabilities and findspans to reader ([@baroquebobcat](https://github.com/baroquebobcat) in [#9578](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9578))

#### 👷 CI Improvements

* Feat(release): draft the github release when the prepare pr merges ([@albertteoh](https://github.com/albertteoh) in [#9740](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9740))
* Ci(backward-compat): build the earlier revision from the latest release tag instead of main ([@alishair7071](https://github.com/alishair7071) in [#9547](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9547))
* Ci(test): raise the storage integration test timeout to 20 minutes ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9680](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9680))
* Ci: check out the default branch explicitly in the pr quota workflow ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9591](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9591))
* Test(integration): support explicit upgrade scenarios in backward-compatibility harness ([@Kartikupadhyay44](https://github.com/Kartikupadhyay44) in [#9566](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9566))

#### ⚙️ Refactoring

* Refactor(memory): give filter values a kind instead of one flag per type ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9677](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9677))
* Refactor(tracestore): make searchdepth and pagesize unsigned on internal query types ([@Kartikupadhyay44](https://github.com/Kartikupadhyay44) in [#9642](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9642))
* Refactor(query): give the query service its own request types ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9654](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9654))
* Refactor(jptrace): share the hex trace and span id parsers ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9632](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9632))
* Refactor(exporter): register jaeger_storage_exporter as a connector with a dead-letter output ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9622](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9622))
* Refactor(storage): export the storage exporter's write core as tracewriter ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9599](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9599))
* Refactor(query): name search query fields in plain english in refusals ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9616](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9616))
* Refactor(query): validate a search query once in the query service alone ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9612](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9612))
* Refactor(storage): generalize paginated reader results ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9585](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9585))

#### 📖 Documentation

* Docs(rfc): mark rfc 0016 m3 delivered ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9759](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9759))
* Docs(rfc): split the deferred kafka consumer milestone into receiver-level batching and a worker pool ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9696](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9696))
* Docs(rfc): record the es/os pagination and tie-breaking decisions for span search ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9691](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9691))
* Docs(rfc): state the single-value rule that attribute ordering must settle ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9679](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9679))
* Docs(rfc): specify caller-selected span ordering ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9667](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9667))
* Docs(rfc): record the delivered rfc 0014 m2 plumbing ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9630](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9630))
* Docs(adr): record synchronous elasticsearch writes and lossless pipelines in adr-014 ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9621](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9621))
* Docs(rfc): propose streaming responses for the api v3 http gateway ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9620](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9620))
* Docs(rfc): compare the clickhouse schema with the clickstack exporter schema ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9596](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9596))
* Docs(rfc): unify paginated reader results ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#9584](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/pull/9584))

### 📊 UI Changes

#### 🐞 Bug fixes, Minor Improvements

* Fix(trace): prevent call-stack overflow on deeply nested traces ([@jkowall](https://github.com/jkowall) in [#4554](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4554))
* Fix(model): align parentage with the backend ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#4569](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4569))
* Fix(jaeger-ui): guard missing array fields in otelspanfacade ([@abhayrajjais01](https://github.com/abhayrajjais01) in [#4323](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4323))
* Fix(dependencygraph): include lookback in view traces url to prevent 400 error. ([@kams19-ops](https://github.com/kams19-ops) in [#4151](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4151))
* Feat(genai): add a json (deep) view that unwraps embedded json ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#4544](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4544))
* Fix(genai): accept bare gen_ai.input and gen_ai.output ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#4542](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4542))
* Fix(flamegraph): preserve search highlighting when collapsing nodes above ([@padmasri-web](https://github.com/padmasri-web) in [#4529](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4529))
* Fix(api/v3): drop out-of-range search timestamps gracefully ([@padmasri-web](https://github.com/padmasri-web) in [#4508](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4508))
* Fix: improve image alt text ([@Piyush4801](https://github.com/Piyush4801) in [#4524](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4524))
* Fix: optimize span index to row index lookup ([@Safian62](https://github.com/Safian62) in [#4500](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4500))
* Fix: correct deep dependencies endpoint ([@Safian62](https://github.com/Safian62) in [#4484](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4484))
* Feat(api/v3): validate v3 trace wire contract at boundary ([@sksingh2005](https://github.com/sksingh2005) in [#4455](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4455))
* Fix(trace-timeline): make span-details divider draggable from the header ([@KKamJi98](https://github.com/KKamJi98) in [#4412](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4412))

#### 👷 CI Improvements

* Feat(release): draft the github release when the prepare pr merges ([@albertteoh](https://github.com/albertteoh) in [#4571](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4571))
* Ci(security): resolve scorecard alerts ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#4557](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4557))
* Ci: check formatting across platforms ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#4495](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4495))

#### ⚙️ Refactoring

* Test(model): materialize otlp trace specs ([@sksingh2005](https://github.com/sksingh2005) in [#4527](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4527))
* Refactor(model): rename trace display helpers ([@ysh-bot](https://github.com/ysh-bot) in [#4573](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4573))
* Refactor(ui): convert deepdependencies to functional component ([@Harizz076](https://github.com/Harizz076) in [#3970](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/3970))
* Chore: drop _get from spantreeoffset hover handlers ([@Priyanshu-byte-coder](https://github.com/Priyanshu-byte-coder) in [#4358](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4358))
* Chore(lint): replace react-x plugin with oxlint's native versions ([@akashchamp](https://github.com/akashchamp) in [#4463](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4463))
* Chore: eliminate as any cast on redux store in app provider (#4333) ([@Kartikupadhyay44](https://github.com/Kartikupadhyay44) in [#4456](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4456))
* Feat(monitor): migrate metrics fetching from redux to react query ([@parshipcy](https://github.com/parshipcy) in [#4048](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4048))
* Refactor(tracepage): decouple graph search logic ([@sksingh2005](https://github.com/sksingh2005) in [#4176](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger-ui/pull/4176))

items.title: Zero-code trace-log correlation with OBI
items.summary: You get paged. A trace shows a request failing in one of your services, and you know the answer is in the logs — but which log lines belong to that request? If the service never adopted structured logging with trace context, the honest answer is: you grep by timestamp and hope. OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation (OBI) can now add that missing trace context to the logs your services already write. Your applications don’t change: no SDK, no logging-library configuration, no application rebuild or redeploy.

items.title: Feedback wanted: Slickfast rendering Grafana panels to images without a browser
items.summary: Hey, everyone. I’m Alex and I built SlickFast, an open-source (AGPL) render engine that turns a JSON chart spec into SVG or PNG without needing a browser. It’s deterministic: the same data always produces byte-identical output. I’ve been testing it against Grafana 13 as a way to get panel images without running a headless browser. A small prototype reads a dashboard and its panel data through the HTTP API (read-only Viewer token), maps core panels to SlickFast charts, and renders the whole board. On Node Exporter Full with real Prometheus data: 124 panels, no unsupported core panels, about 15 ms to render the SVG and 175 ms for a high-resolution PNG. (image) Because it’s just an image, it can go anywhere: alert notifications, email, Slack, e-ink displays, AI agents. The deterministic output also means a report can be fingerprinted and verified later.
